data.title: Hydrocortisone acetate 1% lotion/cream
data.summary: IV Topical corticosteroids · Least potent topical steroid (US class 7; UK 'mild'); non-fluorinated
data.body:
_Topicals · IV Topical corticosteroids_

**Class:** Least potent topical steroid (US class 7; UK 'mild'); non-fluorinated

## Mechanism of action
- Glucocorticoid receptor agonist — mild anti-inflammatory action with very little atrophy

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Face, eyelids, flexures, genitals and nappy area
- Infants and children: mild eczema, seborrhoeic dermatitis, intertrigo
- Maintenance after stronger steroids

## Dose & formulations
- Apply thinly once or twice daily; can be used for longer periods than potent steroids

## Adverse effects
- Very low risk; prolonged use on the face can still cause perioral dermatitis/rosacea
- Contact allergy (tixocortol pivalate group — class A)

## Contraindications
- Untreated infection, rosacea, perioral dermatitis

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Safest steroid for face and infants
- Hydrocortisone is the marker of class A (Coopman) contact allergy

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.45; Khopkar ch.22. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
